newsitem.title: USA: Chase official charged with embezzlement.
newsitem.headline: Chase official charged with embezzlement.

text.p: A senior vice president of Chase Manhattan Corp is charged in a federal complaint with allegedly embezzling $14.5 million from the bank by selling company assets and pocketing some of the proceeds.
A Chase Manhattan spokesman would only say Friday that the executive, senior vice president for global leasing Michael Wachs, has been suspended from his duties.

A spokesman for the U.S. Attorney's office in Manhattan said an investigation is continuing following the arrest of Wachs on October 31. Wachs was released on $1 million personal bond the following day after putting up $250,000 in cash.

According to a complaint signed by Federal Bureau of Investigation agent John Brosnan, Wachs and other individuals "known and unknown" participated in a conspiracy in which three DC-8 airplanes, 485 railroad cars and 338 barges were sold for more than $26.1 million. The complaint said Chase Manhattan received about $11.6 million from the sale and that Wachs "and at least one other individual" profited personally by receiving the $14.5 million differential.
The complaint said that activities in the alleged scheme began around May, 1996 and continued through October.

According to the complaint, an individual identified only as co-conspirator number one at one point purchased $1.4 million in gold Canadian maple leaf coins from Republic National Bank in New York and instructed that they be delivered to Dime Savings Bank in New York where both Wachs and the co-conspirator had leased safe deposit boxes.
On another occasion, according to the complaint, $4.6 million in gold Krugerrands were delivered to Republic where Wachs had 13 safe deposit boxes in his own name.
An attorney representing Wachs was not immediately avaiilable for comment.
A source familiar with the situation said no customers of Chase Manhattan were affected by the alleged scheme, and added that there will be no adverse financial impact on the bank.
Chase Manhattan, with $323 billion in assets at the end of the third quarter, is the largest U.S. bank holding company.
